title: Multiplication Sign: Copy & Paste × Times Symbol
meta_description: Copy and paste the multiplication sign (×) — its 1631 origin, how it differs from the letter x and the dot operator, and how to type it. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
hero_tagline: The × that means "times" — not the letter x — plus the dot and X-mark alternatives it's routinely confused with. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: The multiplication sign (×, Unicode U+00D7) is the dedicated "times" operator used in arithmetic and algebra — 6 × 7, not 6x7. It looks close enough to the Latin letter x that most people type a lowercase x instead, which is why × has its own confusable-neighbors story worth sorting out.
